title: Smt. Nussarat Jahan v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd.
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad, Lucknow Bench
coram: Hon'ble Mrs. Sangeeta Chandra, J.; Hon'ble Brij Raj Singh, J.
disposition: Directed to apply under Paragraph 6.5; coercive recovery stayed if filed within a week.
headnote: A writ for mandamus to correct a meter reading, against a bill the consumer put at Rs.28,579/- and the licensee at Rs.31,546/-, was disposed of by directing an application under Paragraph 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code before opposite party no. 2 within one week, to be decided within three weeks. Coercive recovery of Rs.31,546/- was stayed for five weeks or until that decision, whichever was earlier, and the stay was to lapse if the application was not filed in time.
facts: Smt. Nussarat Jahan petitioned the Lucknow Bench for a mandamus directing U.P. Power Corporation Limited to correct her meter reading in accordance with law. She alleged that the respondents had raised an arbitrary electricity bill of Rs.28,579/- and had not considered her representation. Counsel for the licensee told the Court that a statutory remedy was available under Paragraph 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code and that, after a proper meter reading, the bill stood at Rs.31,546/-.

holding_units.topic: Meter-reading bill dispute relegated to Paragraph 6.5 with a conditional stay of recovery
holding_units.holding: A consumer who seeks mandamus to correct a meter reading and disputes the resulting bill must pursue Paragraph 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code. The writ was disposed of with a direction to file that application before opposite party no. 2 within one week; if filed in time, that authority must complete the applicable formalities and decide it in accordance with the statutory provisions within three weeks. Coercive recovery of Rs.31,546/- stays for five weeks or until the decision, whichever is earlier, and the protection lapses if the application is not filed within one week.

principle_tags.application: The prayer was to correct the meter reading. The consumer alleged a bill of Rs.28,579/-; the licensee said a proper reading produced Rs.31,546/- and invoked Paragraph 6.5. The Court sent the dispute to that remedy.

The writ was disposed of by directing an application under Paragraph 6.5 before opposite party no. 2 within one week, to be decided in accordance with the statutory provisions within three weeks, without a merits finding on the bill.
Coercive recovery of Rs.31,546/- was stayed for five weeks or until the Paragraph 6.5 decision, whichever was earlier, and only if the application was filed within one week.

not_decided.point: Whether the meter reading and the bill of Rs.28,579/- or Rs.31,546/- were correct.
not_decided.note: Left to opposite party no. 2 on a timely application under Paragraph 6.5.
